A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same student-aware reasoning-data selection research despite the changed title. All 20 pages of v1 and 32 pages of v2, including appendices, are readable and support matching methods, experiments, and results. Internal inconsistencies in v2 affect interpretation rather than material completeness.

before.justification: v1 reports original student fine-tuning experiments, teacher and response-selection comparisons, context-window ablations, and math, science, and coding evaluations, including Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains the original fine-tuning results and adds empirical coverage, token-category, and self-conditioning analyses in Sections 5 and 7.4 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: The local scoring formula and highest-score selection rule remain equivalent despite renaming Local Naturalness to LALP. However, v1 Section 3.4 implements steps as individual sentences, whereas v2 Section 6 and Appendix B.1 adopt GLM-4.5-Air to group logical substeps. This changes segmentation and therefore the units being scored, within the retained selection framework.

E1.justification: v2 adds GSM8K to the empirical coverage analysis in Appendix C.6 and Figure 8. The principal training datasets and math benchmarks remain unchanged. GPQA-Diamond, LiveCodeBench, and the 5,000 OpenCodeReasoning/LeetCode training prompts already appeared in v1 Appendix B.5 and are not new coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated selection baselines and external models are retained, including random selection, GRAPE/GALP, Local Lowest, all-teacher training, LIMO-32B, Sky-T1, and OpenThinker2. The Gemma and QwQ sanity checks match across relocated tables. Although v2 Figure 6 omits the random-selection loss curve, Appendix C.1 still reports that comparison.

E3.justification: v2 introduces substantial diagnostic protocols: nearest-neighbor embedding coverage, token-category probability mass over 500 responses, low-probability token analysis over 440 responses, and position-binned probability gaps over approximately 800 responses per teacher. It also describes within-teacher selection as GALP terciles, whereas v1 selects highest, middle, and lowest responses among 16 candidates. v2 Appendix C.9 retains the earlier description, leaving the actual protocol unresolved.

E4.justification: v2 adds step-versus-trajectory coverage analyses, qualitative nearest-neighbor examples, token-attribution analyses, and numerical and stylistic self-conditioning case studies. These investigate mechanisms largely untested in v1. The earlier context-window, teacher-composition, training-loss, and alternative-student analyses remain, although some are redrawn or relocated.

E5.justification: v2 introduces coverage-dispersion summaries, including a range and tenth percentile in Figure 2, and shaded bands in new diagnostic plots. The bands' statistical meaning is unspecified, so they cannot be identified as confidence intervals. Neither version reports training-seed replication or significance tests; the existing eight-sample decoding evaluations are retained.

E6.justification: v2 adds coverage similarities, token-category percentages, probability-gap curves, and qualitative recall findings. The context-window score trend also changes: log probabilities decrease with increasing context in v1 Figure 4 but increase in v2 Figure 3. Established benchmark tables retain their values, including the 32B local/global accuracies of 0.726/0.632 and the science and coding results; these are not new performance gains.

T1.justification: v1 contains scoring definitions but no comparable theoretical development. v2 Appendix A adds a directed-chain model, local-observation and smoothing assumptions, a mixture-minimizer proposition, reasoning-gap and signal-dilution theorems, a local-score robustness theorem, and a corollary with proofs. This substantially expands the formal content beyond restating the scoring equation.

C1.justification: The selection-effectiveness claim and headline accuracy gain remain. However, v2 makes a stronger central explanatory claim: students generalize by recombining familiar steps, and global scoring fails because trajectory fluency is misaligned with transferable reasoning. The abstract and conclusion present this as an identified cause, whereas v1 primarily establishes empirical unreliability and motivates locality more tentatively.

C2.justification: v2 substantially revises the explanation of global scoring's failure, emphasizing coverage granularity, dilution by stylistic tokens, and self-conditioning instead of primarily long-context inconsistency. It adds an explicit limitation that local scoring cannot enforce long-range consistency or detect all propagated early errors, plus qualifications concerning the toy model's Markov and uniform-background assumptions.

D1.justification: v2 supplies the segmentation model and prompt and adds an anonymized code-access link, whereas v1 promises future release. Reported hardware changes from four H100 GPUs or APIs to four A100 GPUs. Conversely, v1's explicit default k=4 and student-specific epoch/learning-rate assignments disappear, although the general hyperparameter tables remain.

R1.justification: v2 substantially broadens positioning around data selection, gradient and influence methods, and reasoning distillation, adding works such as LESS, Select2Reason, Prismatic Synthesis, In Good Graces, and Shape of Thought. It removes v1's explicit grounding in Prystawski et al.'s locality-of-experience work and Lost in the Middle. Publication-year and venue updates for retained references are not counted as new works.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, method exposition, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. The former combined method-and-motivation sequence becomes separate problem-setting, failure, explanation, method, and evaluation sections. Terminology changes to GALP/LALP, detailed results move into the appendix, and an impact/limitations statement replaces the earlier reproducibility statement.

P2.justification: v2 removes the introductory scoring schematic, compresses main-text result tables while retaining full appendix tables, redraws teacher-ranking and context-window plots, and moves/redraws the training-loss figure. It adds coverage, token-category, and self-conditioning plots and qualitative-example tables. Some new displays are mismatched with their descriptions, notably the teacher-selection caption on Table 2's response-selection rows.

improvement.justification: The new theory, mechanism analyses, explicit limitations, segmentation prompt, and code-access link offer substantive benefits. However, important new evidence is internally inconsistent: Figure 2 claims a trajectory-similarity range of 0.68–0.83 while plotting values below 0.5; Table 2 misidentifies response-selection results; and Section 7.3 describes math-to-code transfer while Appendix C.11 retains code-specific fine-tuning. With headline results unchanged and the new protocols and diagnostic evidence unresolved, a reliable net quality improvement cannot be established.
